COMMON QUESTIONS

Frequently Asked Questions About Surety Bonds

Everything you need to know about commercial surety bonds, licensing obligations, rates, and underwriting.

Commercial insurance is a two-party contract designed to protect your business against accidental loss or damage. A Surety Bond is a three-party contract (Principal, Obligee, and Surety) where the surety guarantees to the obligee that the principal will fulfill contractual or legal obligations. If the surety pays a claim, the principal is legally obligated to indemnify the surety.
Bond costs (premiums) are a small percentage of the total bond amount, typically ranging from 0.75% to 2.5% per year for applicants with solid credit. For higher-risk bonds or non-standard credit, rates typically range from 3% to 7%. For example, a standard $10,000 contractor license bond often costs only $100 to $150 per year.
Yes. Surebound partners with specialized non-standard surety markets that evaluate your operational experience, business assets, and references. We offer bad-credit bond programs for almost all license, permit, and commercial bonds.
Most license and permit bonds, notary bonds, and freight broker bonds are issued digitally within minutes upon payment. Complex contract performance bonds can usually be underwritten and approved within 24 to 48 hours.
If a claim is submitted, the surety conducts a thorough investigation to determine its validity. If the claim is valid and the principal does not resolve the issue, the surety settles the claim with the obligee up to the bond penal sum. However, under the General Indemnity Agreement, the principal is legally responsible to reimburse the surety in full.
